browserSearchPath: CLMS Bio-geophysical Parameters, Vegetation, Vegetation Properties
collectionDescription: The Leaf Area Index (LAI) is defined as half the total green canopy area per unit of horizontal ground area. Estimates are produced every 10 days at global scale, at a spatial resolution of approximately 300 m, covering the period from January 2014 to the present.

layers.longDescription: LAI (Leaf Area Index) is defined as half the total area of green elements of the canopy per unit horizontal ground area. It is expressed in m²/m².

layers.shortDescription: Root Mean Square Error on LAI
layers.longDescription: For each dekad, the RMSE (in m²/m²) quantifies the agreement between the final composite LAI value and the individual instantaneous estimates available within the compositing period: the lower the RMSE, the more consistent the dekadal value is with the underlying observations.

layers.shortDescription: Number of valid instantaneous LAI values
layers.longDescription: This quality indicator gives the number of valid instantaneous LAI observations available in the compositing window: the higher the count, the more robust the resulting dekadal estimate generally is.

layers.shortDescription: Length of semi-period before the date
layers.longDescription: Length in days of the semi-period before the dekadal date of the compositing window [days].

layers.shortDescription: Length of semi-period after the date
layers.longDescription: Length in days of the semi-period after the dekadal date of the compositing window [days].

The quality flag (QFLAG) summarises, for each pixel, the status of the Leaf Area Index estimate — for instance whether the value is valid, was derived from a sufficient number of observations, or comes from the backup algorithm — allowing users to filter the dataset according to their quality requirements.
